source.title: Knowledge-Driven Interpretation of Convolutional Neural Networks

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures concept alignment for individual CNN units using segmented-image masks and semantic alignment scores, a different method from feature visualization. Its results show one unit aligned with several concepts, but do not establish that the concepts are unrelated.
record.gate_note: The paper states generally that most units are polysemantic, but its reported example is a single neuron aligned with related building or structure concepts. The circuit-ablation results and learned-direction influence results concern circuits or learned directions, not whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs.
record.test_reason: The paper asserts that most units are polysemantic, offered as motivation for its recall-based σL measure, and reports no rate or data for it. Its results show its alignment framework's outputs: concept counts, circuits, ablation effects and edge weights. The one per-unit example (ResNet-18 unit 196) lists related building and structure concepts, not unrelated inputs. So no result bears on whether any version holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that their ontology-driven framework captures semantic alignment of units and learned directions. They also find semantically related neural circuits whose ablation hurts a few related Places-365 classes and whose directions positively influence each other. They draw no conclusion about how common polysemanticity is.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pixel-level concept masks, WordNet relations, and IoU, F1, or recall-style alignment scores for units and learned directions; it does not reproduce the original feature-visualization method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the number of aligned concepts changes with the alignment threshold and measure (σIoU versus σL); the similarity threshold also changes the number of retrieved circuits.

fits_no_version.finding: For one ResNet-18 unit, σIoU and σL return different top-five concept lists. σL yields more specialized related concepts. The authors say σIoU would ignore secondary concepts of multi-concept units.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Which concepts a CNN unit is credited with, and hence how many, depends on the alignment metric (IoU vs recall). This is close to V7 but not measured as a per-unit polysemanticity rate.

fits_no_version.finding: The number of distinct aligned concepts across units depends strongly on the threshold τ and the metric (Fig. 3). Mask propagation through WordNet adds higher-level concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-alignment counts for CNN units are sensitive to threshold and metric choice. This concerns concept coverage across a layer, not per-unit polysemanticity.

record.problems: The reported individual-neuron example is limited to one unit and related concepts, so it does not establish how often unrelated mixtures occur. The paper also notes that its receptive-field approximation discards effects of striding and padding.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. Circuit-ablation results report effects on Places-365 class accuracy, and learned-direction edge weights report influence between concept-aligned directions; neither measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs.

untested.parts: No measured share or example of units responding to unrelated concepts. The 'most units are polysemantic' statement is asserted without data.
Superposition is not tested as a cause.
Initialization, regularization and training-noise causes are not tested.
AlexNet, ResNet-18 and DenseNet are analysed, but polysemanticity rates are not compared across architectures.
Whether apparent unrelated mixtures share one feature is not tested.
The number of polysemantic units under different measures or activation ranges is not reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'tested' status and its limits_scope label are not supported. The polysemanticity statement (Sec. 3.2) is an unquantified premise for preferring σL. ImageNet results are in supplementary material that is not available here.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not show that any reported neuron responds to unrelated inputs, and does not test the InceptionV1 neuron or the cat-face/car-front/cat-leg example.
Language models and transformer MLP neurons are not studied.
The paper does not test superposition or capacity pressure as the cause of polysemanticity.
The paper does not test initialization, regularization, training noise, or polysemanticity without capacity pressure.

Although it analyzes multiple CNN architectures, it does not compare polysemanticity rates by architecture, activation function, or regularization, or assess reducing such rates without performance loss.
The paper does not test whether apparently unrelated mixtures share a feature or whether unrelated mixtures are rare. Its displayed example contains related concepts.
The paper compares alignment measures, but does not test polysemanticity as a function of activation range or explanation-scoring choices in the sense stated by this version.

rows.subject: ResNet-18, unit 196 in layer4.1
rows.operation_detail: Measured unit-to-concept alignment using σIoU; reported the top five aligned concepts.
rows.note: The five concepts are related building or shelter concepts. This shows multiple concept alignments, but does not demonstrate unrelated inputs.
rows.check: This is an output of the study's own alignment method for one hand-picked unit. The five σIoU concepts (hovel, roof, building, shelter, house) are related within the WordNet taxonomy, so the row cannot show V1's unrelated-input polysemanticity. It should not be linked to V1 or labelled partial.

rows.subject: ResNet-18, unit 196 in layer4.1
rows.operation_detail: Measured unit-to-concept alignment using σL; reported the top five aligned concepts.
rows.note: The paper says σL yields more specialized concepts. These concepts are related structures; the result shows multiple concept alignments but not unrelated inputs.
rows.check: This is the same unit under σL. The concepts (circus tent, greenhouse, shed, pavilion, bandstand) are related structures, and the authors describe them as more specialized concepts within the taxonomy. It is a showcase of the method, not a measurement of polysemanticity, so it is not evidence for V1.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
